set.approach: The crag is a short walk from the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles north parking area, a little north of Bulletproof Rock and close to the bouldering spot called Tin Can Alley, where rusty cans lying about tell you that you are near. The route starts on the right side of the south face, on a vertical white dike.

review.notes: Crag page for location; route page for the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Bear's Behind is a quick walk northwest of The Egg. Sunkiss climbs a smooth slab on the right side of the south face.
set.descent_text: The anchors carry no hardware, so there is nothing to lower from; walk off.

review.notes: Route page states both the start and the walk-off.

set.approach: From the north shore of Big Bear Lake, park where Greenway Drive meets Pioneer Lane and take the trails that wander up the hillside; the formations sit on the south-facing slope above. Big Bubba is the closest formation to the parking: hike uphill, veering right (east) off the approach trail. Dancing Digits is in the center of the southeast face.

review.notes: Approach from area pages. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start from the Pine Creek pack station, where the road ends, and hike the Pine Creek Pass trail uphill. The wall shows up on your left almost beside the path, and since the trail is exposed to sun while the wall is shaded, leaving early is wise. Stepping off the trail at its nearest point to the wall puts you at the left side of the broad buttress. The route starts a short way right of Whats Mine Is Mine.

review.notes: Wall approach from the mine and buttress pages; start from the route page.

set.approach: Bulletproof Rock is a very short walk west and slightly uphill from the circular parking area of the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles north parking area. The route is on the left side of the main face and climbs patina plates to a ramp.

review.notes: Area page for approach; route page for the start.

set.approach: From Highway 18, take the signed trail up to Castle Rock; the hike is uphill. Camelot Crag is just west of Castle Rock, and the route starts to the right of the crack climb Camelot.

review.notes: Castle Rock Area and crag pages; route page for the start.

set.approach: Park at Lake George, walk around the right shore of the lake, and follow the climbers trail to the lowest wall north of Crystal Creek. Staying in or near the creek as long as you can avoids the steep, loose dirt and brush directly below the crag. Bear right and look for the first bolt on a low-angle slab.

review.notes: Crag page. No descent stated.

set.approach: The Lost Universe is a cairned, adventurous hike from the Keller Peak trail starting at yellow-post campsite 7, passing the Crag at the End of the Universe and then working along the ridge through boulders and brush. The East Face is the first wall you reach. It goes up the center of the southeast face, to the right of Silhouette Arete.

review.notes: Lost Universe and East Face pages; route page for the start.

set.approach: Drive Forest Road 2N86 to its end and walk south to the obvious large block, which sits across the road from Castle Grey Skull. The route is on the north face, the side that faces the road.

review.notes: Area page and route page.

set.approach: From the Voodoo Garden parking area hike up toward Slide Dome. Where a few cairns appear, descend and cross the creek, then follow more cairns up the slope on the left, around Bison Crest, and through trees into a field of broken rock; then head east to the foot of the wall. The route is on a vertical, orange-patina wall high in the Voodoo area.

review.notes: Garden Wall page; route page for the wall.

set.approach: Park at Ellery Lake, cross the spillway at the dam, and work straight up the talus field toward the buttress along a faint path. It does not start from the ground: climb Speed of Life's first pitch, belay on the slab left of its midway anchor, and set off up the gently overhanging face to the left.

review.notes: Golden Rock page; route page for the start.

set.approach: High Profile Pinnacle is the last of the roadside formations along forest road 2N13 east of Green Valley Lake, just before the junction with 2N13D, and you can park beside it. The route climbs the arete between Pancho Villa and Tales from Lithuania, starting just left of Pancho Villa.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the top.

review.notes: Area page and route page ("rap anchor").

set.approach: Begin at the Lake George parking area and hike the Crystal Lake trail toward Crystal Crag. The northeast-facing Highlands Wall at the foot of the crag is the first cliff you reach, and it can be seen from the lot. The route starts with a slabby section.
set.descent_text: Lower from the steel carabiners at the anchor.

review.notes: Area pages; route page for descent.
